lines.text: What if you woke up and every other human on Earth had vanished?
Just you, a quiet town by the sea, and the whole planet.

segments.caption: The lights go out
segments.fact: BACKUP FUEL RUNS OUT IN DAYS

lines.text: Within a few days, the power stations' backup generators run dry, and the grid goes dark.
Without electric pumps, the taps soon stop running too.
But the supermarket is full of cans, and low-acid canned food can last two to five years.
After a few months, petrol starts to go stale, and the cars won't start.
So you switch to a bicycle, and a sailboat in the harbour.
But rooftop solar panels still work, and they can keep making power for decades.
With a few batteries, you have light, a fridge and music again.
The biggest threat isn't hunger. It's loneliness.
Long-term loneliness carries a health risk like smoking fifteen cigarettes a day.
So you keep routines, talk out loud, and adopt a stray dog.
When the cans run low, you plant seeds from the garden centre, and learn to farm and fish.
Ten years on, the town is wild and green.
Every night, you climb the lighthouse and switch on its solar light, just in case someone else is out there.
So, would you keep the light on?
